reviewMethod.methodNotesMd: Reviewed the Measure StructureDefinition report, the resource-review context, the deterministic aggregate as prior context only, and direct behavior findings whose `affectedResources` include `Measure`. Shared `Resource` and `DomainResource` behavior findings were treated as context only, not as Measure-specific scoring inputs.

r4Maturity.effectMd: R4 Measure is trial-use/FMM 2, so the compatibility burden is neutral rather than normative. That softens the presumption against redesign, but Measure supports clinical quality measurement, reporting, and payer/provider workflows; lossy documentation/categorization changes and operation-contract breaks still matter when compatibility can be preserved cheaply.

overall.oneLineConclusion: Measure keeps its resource identity, but group-scoped semantics and heavily revised Measure operations make a targeted migration program unavoidable while leaving substantial value in low-cost compatibility preservation.

reasoning.thesisMd: Measure is not removed or replaced, but it is also not a mostly stable R4 resource with a few isolated deltas. The central interpretation fields moved from the root to `Measure.group`, several documentation/categorization paths were removed or restructured, R6 permits population and stratifier definitions without the R4-required criteria expressions, and the primary Measure operations changed routes, selectors, required inputs, and response envelopes. Real implementations therefore need resource and API migration work, but that does not justify avoidable deletions, aliases, or inconsistent operation definitions.
reasoning.migrationShapeMd: The instance-model migration is group-centric: R4 measure-wide scoring/type/compositeScoring/improvementNotation must be copied or mapped into groups, and R6 group-level differences cannot always collapse back to one R4 root value. R4 `definition`, `guidance`, and `topic` need policy-based preservation or mapping. Evaluators also need to handle R6 populations/stratifiers whose criteria are absent because another definition mechanism is used. This is a major targeted remodel rather than a resource-identity break.
reasoning.compatibilityLeverageMd: A Measure migration program is already needed for nontrivial systems, especially systems that implement `$care-gaps`, `$collect-data`, `$evaluate-measure`, or `$submit-data`. Still, compatibility leverage remains high for low-cost measures: deprecated metadata fields, legacy operation routes, legacy selector/filter parameter aliases, reportType alias codes, and corrected operation parameter typing would reduce breakage without blocking the R6 group-centric and Bundle-centric direction. The resource should not be treated as a case where migration dominates so completely that additional breaks no longer matter.
reasoning.lessBreakingAlternativesMd: The most standards-review-worthy alternatives are narrow: retain `Measure.topic` and `Measure.guidance` as deprecated optional fields or define explicit replacements; keep instance invocation or aliases for common Measure operation routes; accept legacy `measure`, `topic`, and `practitioner` selectors while steering clients to canonical R6 selectors; include legacy `reportType` values or weaken the binding during transition; and correct the `$submit-data` `bundle` parameter type. By contrast, some breaks are local migration chores once the R6 redesign is accepted, such as converting `definition` to `term`, parsing Bundle-based operation results, and transforming flat `$submit-data` payloads into per-subject Bundles.
reasoning.behaviorImpactMd: Direct Measure behavior findings materially affect runtime clients and server conformance. The Measure operation family changes request contracts, result envelopes, and route availability; generated clients/servers and validators will require version-specific handling. The single Measure-related search finding is primarily conformance metadata churn from canonical SearchParameter consolidation, not usually a query-code break. Shared Resource/DomainResource behavior findings remain relevant background for generic clients but do not change the Measure resource-level conclusion.
reasoning.comparisonToDeterministicAggregateMd: I agree with the aggregate's broad posture: `Partial` major migration, `major-model-remodel`, and `preserve-where-low-cost-but-expect-resource-migration`. The important nuance is that the conclusion is not count-driven. The root-to-group semantic move and operation-contract churn drive migration, while several Revisit findings remain independently worth preserving or correcting because they are narrow aliases, deprecated fields, or ballot-artifact inconsistencies.
reasoning.uncertaintyMd: Confidence is high for the reported structural and behavior deltas. The main uncertainty is prevalence: FMM 2 Measure content and operations may not be universally deployed, and the reports do not provide official work-group rationale. That uncertainty affects prioritization, not the core conclusion that nontrivial Measure implementations need migration while low-cost compatibility still matters.

findingConsiderations.title: Measure-level scoring, type, compositeScoring, and improvementNotation moved under Measure.group
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This is the central instance-model remodel. It breaks R4 instances carrying measure-wide interpretation metadata and requires group-aware transforms, with lossy R6-to-R4 collapse when groups intentionally diverge.

findingConsiderations.title: Population and value-based stratifier criteria are no longer mandatory in R6
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: Although not an old-valid/new-invalid break, it changes evaluator assumptions and R6-to-R4 representability. Consumers can no longer assume an expression is present and must understand alternate definition mechanisms.

findingConsiderations.title: Measure.topic was removed without a direct R6 replacement
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This is a hard R4 instance break for catalog/search metadata and looks avoidable: a deprecated optional `topic` or explicit replacement path would preserve existing categorizations at low base-model cost.

findingConsiderations.title: Measure.guidance was removed; migration to usage is plausible but lossy
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: Guidance content can be clinically and operationally important. Collapsing it into `usage` is policy-dependent and lossy when both fields exist, so a deprecated field or explicit preservation guidance would be valuable.

findingConsiderations.title: Measure.definition markdown list was replaced by structured Measure.term
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This is a real hard instance break, but the structured `term` model has a coherent R6 goal. It mainly becomes a local transform/rendering chore unless duplicate old/new fields would have been acceptable for one release.

findingConsiderations.title: Measure.subject[x] binding changed and group-level subject scoping was added
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This adds useful group-level subject specificity but creates terminology churn and reverse-conversion loss when group subjects diverge. It contributes to migration complexity without independently making the resource identity unstable.

findingConsiderations.title: Several local string fields changed to markdown primitives
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This affects generated types and rendering, but plain text remains wire-compatible in practice. It should be handled by regeneration and display review, not by resource-level compatibility escalation.

findingConsiderations.title: R6 adds Measure-specific constraints for related artifacts, linkIds, and basisRequirement
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: The reported constraints are warnings or apply to new R6-only content. They do not materially change the R4-to-R6 instance migration posture.

findingConsiderations.title: R6 replaces the R4 topic/subject request contract with required measureUrl and status inputs
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: The same operation family now requires different measure selection and status inputs. R4 clients using topic/subject selectors need business mapping, so Measure API migration is unavoidable for care-gaps users.

findingConsiderations.title: R6 changes successful responses from a direct Bundle to Parameters containing repeated return Bundles
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This is a hard client response-shape break. It is partly justified by multiple returned Bundles, but a single-Bundle compatibility mode would be worth considering for transition.

findingConsiderations.title: Instance-level Measure/$collect-data invocation is removed
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: Dropping the instance route is an avoidable runtime/API break. The R6 canonical selector goal can coexist with `[base]/Measure/{id}/$collect-data` as a deprecated compatibility route that infers the selected Measure.

findingConsiderations.title: The `measure` selector is replaced by required repeatable `measureUrl` canonical values
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: Canonical `measureUrl` is reasonable, but retaining the R4 `measure` selector as a single-measure alias would preserve common clients with modest resolution and precedence rules.

findingConsiderations.title: Output changes from measureReport plus resource parts to repeatable return Bundles
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This drives client migration, but the old flat output shape is a poor fit for per-subject and multi-measure bundles. It is mainly a local operation migration chore once the R6 result model is accepted.

findingConsiderations.title: R6 rendered pages mix stale and undeclared parameter names with the computable definition
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This is not a necessary migration burden; it is an avoidable specification artifact inconsistency. Correcting the narrative or formal aliases has low cost and high conformance value.

findingConsiderations.title: Type-level measure selection no longer accepts the R4 string/reference measure parameter
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: The R6 canonical and inline Measure selection goals are sound, but the old type-level selector could be retained as a deprecated alias. This is a low-cost preservation opportunity despite the operation's broader redesign.

findingConsiderations.title: reportType changes from unbound legacy prose codes to a required R6 evaluation-type binding
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This makes R4-documented values computably invalid while narrative compatibility expects support for them. Deprecated alias codes or a transitional weaker binding would align validators with the intended compatibility story.

findingConsiderations.title: The operation result changes from one direct MeasureReport to repeated Bundle returns in a Parameters envelope
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: The response-shape migration is large, but the Bundle model carries evaluated/created resources more coherently. This supports the conclusion that API migration is needed, while not necessarily requiring standards reversal.

findingConsiderations.title: R6 removes the Measure instance-level $submit-data endpoint
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: The type-level or root Bundle direction is understandable, but a deprecated instance route for single-measure R4 workflows would preserve existing integrations with limited server-routing cost.

findingConsiderations.title: R6 replaces flat measureReport/resource inputs with a required repeating bundle input
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This is a hard request-body break, but grouped Bundles are a coherent R6 model for multi-subject and multi-measure submission. It is mostly a planned migration task rather than a low-cost preservation candidate.

findingConsiderations.title: R6 names the input bundle but formally types it as MeasureReport while the narrative/example use Bundle
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This is a standards artifact inconsistency, not a justified redesign. Aligning the formal type with the intended Bundle payload is low-cost and important for validators and generated clients.

findingConsiderations.title: R6 consolidates many per-resource canonical SearchParameter URLs into multi-base CanonicalResource and MetadataResource definitions
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: For Measure this is mainly conformance metadata churn: the query codes can remain usable, but canonical SearchParameter identity changes affect CapabilityStatement comparison and generators. Deprecated aliases would be helpful but it does not drive Measure instance migration.

findingConsiderations.title: R6 invocation matrix changes instance-level Resource $validate request semantics
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This may affect generic validators used with Measure, but it is a shared Resource behavior finding. Per the review rules it provides background only and is not scored as a Measure-specific change.

findingConsiderations.title: Core special/profile search parameters changed type metadata for _content, _text, _query, and _profile
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This can affect generic search tooling around Measure resources, but it is assigned to Resource/DomainResource shared behavior rather than Measure-specific semantics.

recommendedNextActions.actionMd: Create a Measure migration guide that separates instance transforms from operation/API transforms: root-to-group metadata mapping, `definition` to `term`, `guidance`/`topic` preservation policy, optional criteria handling, and Bundle-based operation request/response parsing.

Raise standards follow-up for low-cost compatibility preservation: deprecated `topic` and `guidance`, legacy Measure operation routes and selector/filter aliases, legacy `reportType` values, and the `$submit-data` `bundle` formal type mismatch.
For servers and SDKs, provide version-aware adapters for `$care-gaps`, `$collect-data`, `$evaluate-measure`, and `$submit-data` rather than relying on OperationDefinition regeneration alone.

When comparing R4 and R6 search support for Measure, match by base/code/type/expression in addition to canonical SearchParameter URL, and consider advertising deprecated canonical aliases where conformance tooling depends on exact URLs.

caveats: The review uses R4 FMM/status as the compatibility baseline; R6 maturity/status was not used to increase or lower the burden.
Shared Resource and DomainResource behavior findings were considered only as context because the assigned resource is Measure, not Resource or DomainResource.
The reports provide high-confidence structural and operation deltas, but not definitive work-group rationale or deployment prevalence.
